disagreements.topic: Target multiple (the main remaining fair-value spread, $262-277)
disagreements.positions: agents 3 and 4: 9.0x; agent_2: 9.25x; agents 1 and 5: 9.5x, all on NTM EPS of ~$29.0-29.4. After-SBC FCF yields are 9.25-9.5% in all five.
disagreements.resolution: About 9.1x. Today the stock trades at ~8.8x NTM, and the sell-side has not cut FY27 EPS since the Wadhwani news: consensus is still $27.62-27.67 (MarketBeat and StockAnalysis). The EPS base therefore carries downside risk at the Dec ~9 guide, and a multiple much above today's would stack a re-rating on top of possibly stale numbers. Jefferies expects more senior departures, and the board already put retention letters in place in July. I see nothing before December that would drive a re-rating.
disagreements.evidence: MarketBeat forecast page (FY27 $27.62); Jefferies note via FinanceFeeds (PT $285 to $275, 'more departures and organizational changes are likely'); Adobe 8-K filed Jul 17, 2026 (retention letter, protections sunset 12 months after the new CEO starts).

disagreements.topic: Whether leadership turnover and the organic net-new-ARR decline justify the gap to fair value staying open
disagreements.positions: All five put the 12-month median at $245-254, 3-7% above spot and 6-10% below their own fair values (mean $269). agent_3 closes the most (median ~97% of FV) and agent_4 the least (~93%).
disagreements.resolution: Mostly yes, keep the gap. (1) The turnover is broad: CEO change Dec 1, interim CFO, and the head of ~3/4 of revenue gone Sep 27 with no successor named. No 8-K has been filed since Sep 10, so no replacement has been announced. A new CEO's first guide carries elevated reset risk, and consensus FY27 EPS has not moved. (2) Q3 organic net new ARR fell ~37% y/y. The guide only implies an easing to ~-16% in Q4, and that is not delivered until ~Dec 9. (3) The offsetting floor is real: ~9% after-SBC FCF yield, ~7%/yr share shrink and net debt of ~$0.7B. Adobe's only previous CEO handover (Dec 2007) was followed by a 50% fall, but that coincided with the 2008 crash and is a sample of one, so I give it no weight. Net, a median ~$249 (~40% of the gap closed in 12 months) is right. I would not close more of the gap before the December guide, nor less given the valuation floor.
disagreements.evidence: EDGAR 8-K list for CIK 796343 (latest Sep 10, 2026); Sep 8, 2026 8-K Item 5.02; Q3 FY26 call (Evercore -36-37%); Yahoo Finance Sep 8, 2026 on the 2007 handover; Jefferies via FinanceFeeds.

confidence_reason: The round-2 forecasts converged because they adopted my round-1 corrections. My new checks found no fact that clearly moves the 12-month distribution away from their mean: consensus EPS has not been cut, no successor has been named, and the only Adobe CEO-transition precedent is confounded by 2008. The leadership and bookings evidence explains why the median sits well below fair value, which the agents already reflect, so I keep the mean ladder.
thesis_break_reason: Below ~$178, about 6% under the June 2026 low of ~$190 and ~6.4x FY27 consensus EPS despite a ~9% after-SBC FCF yield and ~7%/yr share shrink, the market would be pricing a cut in earnings power rather than a lower multiple. Examples: a December FY27 guide from the new CEO implying low-single-digit organic ARR growth, Q4 net new ARR well below the guide-implied ~$0.78B, a margin reset, or further senior departures from the Creative business.
key_drivers: The ~Dec 9 Q4 FY26 print and FY27 guide, the first under CEO Chakravarthy (starts Dec 1), with an interim CFO and no named successor to Wadhwani, who ran ~3/4 of revenue. Consensus FY27 EPS ($27.62-27.67) has not yet been cut.
Organic net new ARR: -37% y/y in Q3. The FY 10.2% ARR guide implies Q4 ~$0.78B (~-16% y/y). Missing that figure is the main path to the thesis break.
Valuation floor: ~8.8x NTM EPS, ~9.1% after-SBC FCF yield, net debt ~$0.7B, and a ~$2.2B/quarter buyback taking the share count from 389M to ~363M.
Competitive evidence: Figma +48%; Canva ~$4B annualized revenue with in-house models cutting AI serving costs ~90%. The AI-disruption rotation dominates the multiple.
Further org change: Jefferies expects more departures, and retention letters (Jul 2026) show the board anticipated attrition.

fair_value.reason: Blend of (a) NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep 2027 of ~$29.3 (2/12 FY27 $27.67 + 10/12 FY28 ~$30.0, trimmed ~1% for December reset risk) x 9.1x = ~$267 and (b) after-SBC FCF of ~$9.1B (TTM $8.47B grown ~7.5%) on ~363M shares = ~$25.1/share at a 9.4% yield = ~$267. Net debt of ~$0.7B is immaterial. This is ~$2 below the agents' round-2 mean ($269.4). I hold the multiple and yield at roughly today's level (8.8x / 9.1%) rather than the 9.5x used by agents 1 and 5, because consensus EPS has not absorbed the leadership turnover.

summary: All five agents took the round-1 fixes (fiscal-year EPS weighting, after-SBC FCF, a 362-365M share count), and their fair values have converged to $262-277 (mean $269). My fair value is ~$267, at roughly today's multiple, because consensus FY27 EPS has not been cut for the turnover. The gap between that fair value and the ~$249 median forecast (spot $238) is justified: the new CEO gives his first guide ~Dec 9 with an interim CFO and no named head for the Creative business (~3/4 of revenue), and organic net new ARR fell 37% in Q3. That risk is offset by a ~9% after-SBC FCF yield and a ~7%/yr share shrink. I keep the forecasters' mean ladder (P(>=spot) ~55%) with low confidence, and suggest a small position built in two tranches, with the second after the December guide.

sizing.reason: The valuation floor is real (~9x EPS, ~9% after-SBC FCF yield, heavy buyback), but the expected 12-month edge is modest (median ~$249, ~+5%) against ~40% volatility. A binary-ish December guide from a new CEO with an interim CFO and no Creative head could send the stock to the high $100s. Since it would be the only position in an all-cash portfolio, I cap it at 6%, down from 8% in round 1 now that fair values have converged lower (~$267-269 vs ~$272-281). Liquidity is not a constraint.
